about.title: Modesto Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing someone suddenly on a Modesto road leaves a family with grief first and paperwork second. Public records for 2025 count 20 traffic deaths in the city, alongside 1,365 injury collisions that left 1,992 people hurt. A wrongful death claim is the civil side of what follows. It runs separately from any criminal case, and it exists so surviving spouses, domestic partners, children, and certain dependent heirs can recover funeral and burial costs, the financial support the person would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. California generally allows two years from the date of death to file, though that window shrinks considerably when a government entity is involved, so timing matters more than most families realize. Collisions here cluster along Coffee Road, Oakdale Road, Tully Road, and Briggsmore Avenue, often on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. LawProactive is not a law firm. We simply connect Modesto families with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: What Modesto Families Should Know Before Filing

items.title: Not everyone can bring the claim
items.desc: California gives first standing to a spouse or registered domestic partner and the children, with certain dependents and heirs able to step in only in specific situations. An attorney can sort out who in your family is eligible before anything is filed.

items.title: The clock runs from the date of death
items.desc: Most wrongful death actions must be filed within two years of the death, but if a city, county, or state agency may share responsibility, a much shorter administrative deadline applies. Starting early protects your family's position.

items.title: The losses the law recognizes
items.desc: A claim can cover funeral and burial expenses, the income and support your loved one would have contributed, and the loss of their companionship, care, and guidance. It is a civil matter and proceeds independently of any criminal prosecution.

items.question: My brother was killed in a crash on Briggsmore Avenue and the other driver is facing charges. Do we have to wait for the criminal case?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action, and it proceeds on its own track regardless of what happens in the criminal court. In fact, waiting can be risky because the two-year civil deadline keeps running while the criminal case unfolds. An attorney can coordinate with the district attorney's timeline while protecting your family's claim.

items.question: My parents were never married but lived together for decades. Can my mother file for my father's death?
items.answer: It depends on whether they were registered domestic partners under California law, which is treated the same as a marriage for standing purposes. If they were not registered, she may still qualify as a dependent under certain conditions, though the analysis is more involved. This is exactly the kind of question worth putting to an independent attorney early, and children of the deceased typically have standing in their own right.
